etymology: Medieval Latin algorismus, from the name of the 9th-century Persian mathematician al-Khwarizmi. In modern English the word names a finite, rule-governed procedure for calculation or decision — especially the procedures that rank, filter, and recommend what a screen shows a man.
biblical_def: An algorithm is a set of steps that turns inputs into an output. Scripture never uses the word, but it does name the thing the age now hides behind the word: a rule of judgment. Scales, lots, weights, and written statutes are older algorithms — public, inspectable, answerable to the LORD. A just weight is His delight (Prov 11:1). The danger is not calculation; it is the transfer of trust from the LORD who directs paths (Prov 3:5-6) to a procedure that cannot love, cannot fear God, and cannot give account. Human hearts still plan their way; the LORD still directs steps (Prov 16:9). No ranking engine is wiser than its makers, and its makers are not wiser than God.

corruption_summary: The age treats “the algorithm” as a neutral oracle — objective, authorless, and therefore unjudgeable — so that ranking, rationing, and silencing can hide behind math.
corruption_paragraphs: Silicon Valley and the platforms speak of the algorithm the way pagans spoke of fate: impersonal, inevitable, and conveniently without a name to summon. A procedure written by men, trained on men’s clicks, and tuned to men’s profit is then preached as if it were nature. That is a redefinition. An algorithm is not weather. It is a human rule of judgment, and every human rule of judgment is moral.

The second inversion is trust. Lean not on your own understanding becomes lean on the feed. Counsel, elders, Scripture, and a man’s own conscience are displaced by a ranking that was never ordained as a magistrate. Recover the older honesty: name the makers, name the aim, and try every procedure by the same law that tries a false balance.
roots_summary: No biblical Hebrew or Greek lemma equals algorithm. The nearest canonical analogs are public measures of judgment — scales, lots, and statutes — not invented Strong’s numbers.
roots_lines: Arabic al-Khwarizmi — the mathematician whose name became medieval algorismus, then English algorithm.
Latin regula / English rule — a procedure is a rule of working; Scripture already judges rules by whether they are just.
No Strong’s number assigned — the word is post-biblical; do not force a Hebrew or Greek tag onto a modern technical noun.
usage: An algorithm is a human rule of judgment written in steps; it is not an authorless god.
Trust the LORD with all your heart; do not outsource wisdom to a ranking engine.
If the procedure cannot be inspected, it cannot be a just weight.

etymology: Latin inflatio, from inflare — to blow into, to swell. In economics, the swelling of the money supply so that the same coin buys less. In older moral speech, also the swelling of pride.
biblical_def: Inflation, as a money-word, is the cheapening of the measure. The LORD hates a false balance and delights in a just weight (Prov 11:1). Israel was forbidden injustice in length, weight, or volume, and commanded honest scales because the LORD had brought them out of Egypt (Lev 19:35-36). When silver becomes dross and wine is mixed with water (Isa 1:22), the people have not suffered a mysterious climate of prices; they have suffered debasement. Amos names the same sin from the seller’s side: shrinking the ephah, enlarging the shekel, falsifying the scales by deceit (Amos 8:5). A currency that is quietly thinned is a false weight with a national stamp.

corruption_summary: Modern speech treats inflation as weather — a nameless “rise in prices” — so that the thinning of the measure is no longer named as a false weight.
corruption_paragraphs: Central-bank English and news-ticker English have redefined inflation as something that happens to an economy, like rain. The older moral fact is that someone altered the measure. If the ephah is made small and the shekel large, that is deceit whether the tool is a merchant’s thumb or a printing press. Calling the result “headline CPI” does not baptize the scales.

A second corruption is to treat inflation as a mere policy lever for growth, as if stealing a little from every wage and every widow’s savings were prudence. Scripture’s category remains abomination: dishonest scales. Recover the word as a justice-word, not a weather-word.
roots_summary: No single biblical lemma equals the modern economic noun. The governing canonical category is the false weight / debased silver.
roots_lines: Latin inflare — to blow into; the image is swelling, not creating substance.
Hebrew analog: dishonest scales and debased silver (Prov 11:1; Isa 1:22) — no invented Strong’s tag on the English noun.
The moral root is theft by measure, not a mysterious rise in “the price level.”
usage: Inflation is a swollen measure: the same coin, less bread.
A just weight is the LORD’s delight; a thinned currency is a false balance with a flag on it.
Do not call debasement weather.

etymology: Portmanteau of bit (binary digit) and coin, coined in the 2008–2009 white paper published under the name Satoshi Nakamoto. A software-scarce digital unit transferred on a public ledger without a central issuer.
biblical_def: Bitcoin is a modern instrument of exchange and speculation. Scripture does not name it, and this dictionary will not pretend the apostles mined blocks. What Scripture does name is the heart’s relation to money. No one can serve God and mammon (Matt 6:24). The love of money is a root of all kinds of evil (1 Tim 6:10). Wealth gained by dishonesty shrinks; labor gathered honestly increases (Prov 13:11). Where the treasure is, the heart follows (Matt 6:21). A scarce ledger may be a wiser measure than a thinned fiat coin, or it may be a new casino with a piety of “freedom.” The test is not the cryptography. The test is whether the unit is used as a just weight in honest trade, or as a rival lord.

corruption_summary: Bitcoin is preached on one side as messianic salvation from the state, and on the other as mere gambling — both of which dodge the older questions of mammon, measure, and honest labor.
corruption_paragraphs: Libertarian gospel-talk baptizes a protocol as if scarcity itself were righteousness. A ledger can refuse a central printer and still be served as mammon. Number-go-up is not the kingdom. The opposite error is equally lazy: treating every non-fiat unit as a scam so that the existing false weight never has to be named. Neither slogan is a biblical definition.

Recover the instrument as an instrument. Ask whether it is used in honest exchange, whether it trains greed or stewardship, and whether the heart can lay it down. Christ is Lord of the wallet that holds sats the same as the wallet that holds paper.
roots_summary: Modern coinage. The governing biblical lemma is not a crypto-word but mammon — money as rival master.
roots_lines: English bit + coin — 2008–2009 coinage; no 1828 entry to quote.
Greek mammonas (G3126) — wealth personified as a master (Matt 6:24); this is the canonical category, not a forced “bitcoin” root.
No Hebrew lemma. Do not invent a Strong’s number for a 21st-century ticker.
usage: Bitcoin is a ledger-unit; it is not a savior.
A scarce coin can still be mammon if the heart kneels to it.
Test the wallet by Matthew 6:21, not by the chart.

etymology: Portmanteau of deep learning and fake, popularized c. 2017 for synthetic audio or video generated to impersonate a real person’s face, voice, or acts.
biblical_def: A deepfake is a manufactured likeness presented as a witness of what happened. The ninth commandment already forbids false witness; the second commandment already forbids making a likeness to serve a lie. “You shall not make for yourself a carved image” (Exod 20:4) is not a ban on every picture, but it does name the danger of an image that claims what is not true. Lying lips are an abomination to the LORD (Prov 12:22). Satan does not stand in the truth; when he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own resources, for he is a liar and the father of it (John 8:44). The lawless one comes with lying wonders (2 Thess 2:9). A synthetic face is a new tool for an old father.

Lying lips are an abomination to the LORD, But those who deal truthfully are His delight.
John 8:44

2 Thessalonians 2:9
The coming of the lawless one is according to the working of Satan, with all power, signs, and lying wonders.
corruption_summary: The word is used both to name a real forgery and to un-name every inconvenient video as “probably fake” — a solvent poured on all testimony.
corruption_paragraphs: Deepfake technology is a genuine instrument of false witness: a face and a voice made to confess what the person never said. That is the first corruption of image — likeness detached from truth. The second corruption is cultural: once the public learns that any clip can be cooked, the guilty party need only shrug “deepfake” and the ninth commandment is inverted. False witness now wears the costume of skepticism.

Recover two duties at once. Do not make or spread a synthetic likeness as if it were a record. And do not use the possibility of forgery as a universal acid against every true report. The LORD still delights in those who deal truthfully. Lying wonders do not cancel the duty to weigh witnesses; they raise it.
roots_summary: Modern coinage. Canonical analogs are image / likeness and lie / false witness — not a invented Greek for “neural net.”
roots_lines: English deep (deep learning) + fake — 2017 coinage; no Webster 1828 lemma.
Greek eikon (G1504) — image, likeness; the second-commandment danger is a likeness pressed into false worship or false witness.
No Strong’s number for deepfake itself. Omit rather than invent.
usage: A deepfake is false witness wearing a stolen face.
Do not let “it could be fake” become a solvent for every true testimony.
Lying wonders are old; the camera is new.

etymology: French surveillance, from surveiller — to watch over (sur- over + veiller to watch, from Latin vigilare). The systematic watching of persons, places, or communications, usually by a power that can record and act.
biblical_def: Surveillance is watching-as-power. God’s watching is holy: He searches and knows, understands the thought afar off, and is acquainted with all our ways (Ps 139:1-4). No creature is hidden from His sight; all things are naked and open to the eyes of Him to whom we must give account (Heb 4:13). The eyes of the LORD are in every place, keeping watch on the evil and the good (Prov 15:3). That omniscience belongs to God, not to Caesar, not to a platform, and not to a jealous spouse with a tracker. Magistrates may watch in order to punish evil and praise good; that is a limited, lawful seeing. When seeing becomes a substitute for God’s throne — secret, total, and unaccountable — it is a stolen attribute.

corruption_summary: The age splits the word in two false directions: total state/platform seeing as safety, and absolute privacy as if a man were not already naked before God.
corruption_paragraphs: Security-state English and advertising English both covet omniscience. Cameras, logs, and ranking engines are preached as care. That is a redefinition of watch: the watchman of Scripture warns and gives account; the modern apparatus records in secret and sells or coerces. A magistrate’s limited sight for public justice is not the same thing as a panopticon that wants every word on the tongue.

The equal-and-opposite corruption is the gospel of absolute privacy — as if the highest good were to be unseen. A man is already seen. Recover both truths: fear the LORD who sees in secret, and refuse any creature that claims His eyes without His holiness or His limits.
roots_summary: French/Latin watching-over. The biblical analog is the LORD’s seeing and the office of watchman — not a fabricated Strong’s tag on the French noun.
roots_lines: French surveiller — to watch over; English borrowed the noun for systematic observation.
Latin vigilare — to keep watch; related English vigil, vigilant.
No Strong’s number for surveillance. God’s seeing in Ps 139 and Heb 4:13 is the doctrinal control, not a forced lemma.
usage: God’s seeing is holy omniscience; creaturely surveillance is a limited power that must stay under law.
A watchman warns; a panopticon hoards.
Do not call total logging care, and do not call hiding from God freedom.

etymology: Latin propagare, to spread, propagate. In 1622 the Roman Congregatio de Propaganda Fide (Congregation for Propagation of the Faith) gave the word its institutional career. Later English made it the name for organized persuasion, especially the organized lie.
biblical_def: Propaganda is speech organized to move a people, with truth treated as optional. Scripture already knows the thing: circulating a false report, joining the wicked as an unrighteous witness (Exod 23:1); the false witness who utters lies (Prov 14:5); prophets who speak a vision of their own heart, not from the mouth of the LORD (Jer 23:16); those who call evil good and good evil (Isa 5:20). Preaching is not propaganda. Preaching is bound to a text, a God, and a judgment. Propaganda is bound to an outcome. The difference is not volume or repetition. The difference is whether the speaker is a witness or a handler.

corruption_summary: Two inversions now own the word: every unpopular truth is smeared as “propaganda,” and every branded campaign is baptized as mere “messaging.”
corruption_paragraphs: Postmodern usage turns propaganda into a tribal insult. If the other side said it, it is propaganda; if our side said it, it is narrative, framing, or public health. That is not a definition. It is a way to stop weighing witnesses. Isaiah 5:20 still names the act: calling evil good and good evil.

The professional inversion is smoother: ministries of information, wartime offices, and corporate “comms” treat organized persuasion as a neutral craft. Technique without the ninth commandment is still false witness when it circulates a false report. Recover the older line: a faithful witness does not lie, even when the lie would win the hour.
roots_summary: Latin propagare (to spread). Biblical control-words are false report, false witness, and the prophet who speaks from his own heart.
roots_lines: Latin propagare — to spread abroad; 1622 de Propaganda Fide made the gerund a proper name.
English then darkened the noun toward organized persuasion detached from truth.
No Strong’s number for the Latin institutional term. Canonical lemmas stay with false witness / false prophet, not an invented tag.
usage: Propaganda organizes speech toward an outcome; preaching is bound to a text.
Calling every rival claim “propaganda” is itself a way of circulating a false report.
A faithful witness does not lie, even when the lie would mobilize the crowd.

etymology: Greek porne (harlot, female prostitute) + graphein (to write, to depict). 19th-century learned English for writings and pictures of sexual immorality; now the industrial depiction of fornication and adultery for consumption.
biblical_def: Pornography is lust made into a product: the harlot written, drawn, filmed, and sold so that a man may commit adultery in his heart on demand. Jesus does not wait for the body: whoever looks at a woman to lust for her has already committed adultery with her in his heart (Matt 5:27-28). Job made a covenant with his eyes (Job 31:1). God’s will is sanctification: abstain from sexual immorality; possess your own vessel in honor, not in passion of lust like the Gentiles who do not know God (1 Thess 4:3-5). Do not lust after her beauty in your heart (Prov 6:25). Fire taken to the bosom still burns (Prov 6:27). The screen does not create a third category between chastity and porneia. It is porneia with a pause button.

corruption_summary: The trade renamed itself “adult content” and “sex positivity,” turning porneia into a wellness good and the seventh commandment into a taste.
corruption_paragraphs: Industrial pornography is not a private aesthetic. It is fornication and adultery of the heart, packaged, priced, and discipled into habit. The modern redefinition calls it content, expression, or even therapy. Scripture’s name does not move: sexual immorality, lust, adultery in the heart. Consent between the camera and the consumer does not un-sin the look.

A second inversion is to treat the image as victimless because no body in the room was touched. Jesus locates the sin in the look. Job locates the guard at the eyes. Recover the covenant with the eyes, the honor of one’s own vessel, and the old word porneia — not the industry’s softer brands.
roots_summary: Greek porne + graphein. The New Testament control-word is porneia (G4202), sexual immorality — not a separate modern virtue called “adult content.”
roots_lines: Greek porneia (G4202) — sexual immorality, fornication; the NT’s governing noun for the thing pornography depicts and sells.
Greek graphein — to write or depict; the “-graphy” is the making of the sin into an image.
No additional invented Strong’s number for the 19th-century English compound.
usage: Pornography is porneia written and sold; the pause button does not make it chaste.
Adultery in the heart does not require a second body in the room.
Make a covenant with your eyes; do not buy the harlot’s picture.

etymology: Latin addictio, from addicere — to award, to sentence, to bind over. Older English could mean a devoted binding (see the KJV’s addicted of Stephanas). Modern English narrowed it to compulsive bondage, especially to a substance or a practiced lust.
biblical_def: Addiction, in the modern sense, is being brought under the power of a thing so that it reigns. Paul will not be brought under the power of any (1 Cor 6:12). Sin must not reign in the mortal body so that you obey it in its lusts; sin shall not have dominion over you (Rom 6:12, 14). False teachers promise liberty while they themselves are slaves of corruption: by whom a person is overcome, by him also he is brought into bondage (2 Pet 2:19). Wine-lingering already has a biblical case study in woe, sorrow, and wounds without cause (Prov 23:29-30). The dictionary already honors the older KJV sense under addicted — a glad giving of the self to ministry. This entry names the other pole: the self handed over to a master that is not the LORD.

For sin shall not have dominion over you, for you are not under law but under grace.
2 Peter 2:19
While they promise them liberty, they themselves are slaves of corruption; for by whom a person is overcome, by him also he is brought into bondage.
corruption_summary: Therapeutic English made addiction a disease-identity that dissolves agency, while pop culture made it a quirky brand — both of which dodge Scripture’s words: lust, dominion, bondage, and repentance.
corruption_paragraphs: The medical file may describe a real bodily slavery; this dictionary does not deny that a man can be overcome. The corruption is the redefinition of the sinner into a mere patient whose craving is an identity and whose repentance is pathologized as shame. Scripture still commands: do not let sin reign; do not present your members to it; you are not under its dominion because you are under grace. Bondage is real. So is the call to come out.

The commercial inversion is lighter and just as false: “I’m addicted to” as branding for appetites we refuse to mortify. Recover the two poles the language already has. Holy addiction is Stephanas giving himself to the saints. Unholy addiction is a master that is not Christ. Grace does not baptize the tyrant. It dethrones him.
roots_summary: Latin addicere (to bind over). Canonical control-words are dominion, lust, and bondage — not an invented Greek for the modern clinical noun. See also addicted for the KJV’s older devoted sense.
roots_lines: Latin addicere / addictio — to sentence or bind over; older English kept the devoted sense, modern English kept the enslaved sense.
New Testament analog: being brought under the power of a thing (1 Cor 6:12) and sin’s reign (Rom 6:12-14). No invented Strong’s number for the English clinical noun.
Related entry addicted treats the KJV commendation of Stephanas; this noun treats the bondage sense the age actually searches.
usage: Addiction in the modern sense is a master: by whom a man is overcome, by him he is brought into bondage.
Do not let the disease-label cancel the command that sin shall not reign.
Holy devotion and unholy bondage both bind; only one binds to the LORD.
